elements.element: Governing law is the laws of the State of New York
elements.evidence: "governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York"

elements.element: Exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County
elements.evidence: "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction"

elements.element: Governing law and forum form a permitted corresponding pair (no conflicting foreign law/forum left standing)
elements.evidence: Singapore law and "the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction" deleted from 28.1

elements.element: Delaware or California law with corresponding Delaware/California courts
elements.evidence: Clause selects "the laws of the State of New York" and New York County courts, not a fallback jurisdiction

elements.element: Alternatively, laws of England and Wales with the courts of London
elements.evidence: No reference to England and Wales or London courts

reasons: Preferred level is fully achieved: New York governing law in 28.1 paired with the pre-existing exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County in 28.2, with the conflicting Singapore law and Singapore forum wording removed.
Fallback is not satisfied (and need not be), as the clause sits at the preferred New York pair rather than Delaware/California or England and Wales/London.

The second operation, narrowing the temporary injunctive-relief carve-out from "another court with jurisdiction" to "those courts", was not required to complete the preferred position; the exclusive-jurisdiction sentence already stood and the carve-out is a mutual, untouched commercial term. This extra edit also removes our own ability to seek urgent relief where assets or infringers sit, so it is an unnecessary change beyond the rule.
Intent is otherwise preserved: no undefined terms, contradictions, or dangling mechanics; personal jurisdiction and venue-waiver language remain effective.
